title: A layer being used as a mask says so in the Layers list
goal: When one layer is cut to the shape of the layer under it, that lower layer stops being drawn and becomes the shape instead. Right now it simply vanishes from the picture while its row in the Layers list looks exactly as it did, thumbnail and all, so the only way to find out where your rectangle went is to undo. Make the row say it.
notes:
Found while building layers-combine-over-the-tracks-below-them (2026-09-21). Reproduction: open any picture, unlock it, draw a rectangle with R, send it to the back with shift-cmd-[, select the picture and set Masked by to Its shape. The rectangle disappears from the canvas; its row still shows a red thumbnail and nothing else. queue/audits/2026-09-21-layers-combine-matte.png is the state.

The model already knows: PhotonzDocument.isSpentAsAMatte(_:) in Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerCompositing.swift answers it for any layer id, and the renderer uses exactly that rule to skip drawing it (DocumentRenderer.compositeLayers). The work is a LayerPanelRow field plus the row UI in the layers panel.
acceptance: A layer that is being spent as the mask of the layer above it is marked as such in the Layers list, without a person having to select anything
The mark says which layer is using it, or the layer above says which layer it is borrowing from, so the pair can be read off the list
Turning the mask off puts the row straight back to normal
A layer that is not being used as a mask looks exactly as it does today

log.note: Reproduced first: ran layers-combine-walk before touching anything. At stage 6-matte the canvas showed the keyed subject cut to the plate's brightness with the plate gone, and the Rectangle row still read plain 'layer' with a full red thumbnail. That is the bug exactly as filed.

Adversarial review before building: (1) a mark on the spent row alone is a dead end, since you still have to work out who took it, so BOTH rows carry a line and each names the other; (2) the line has to follow the PICTURE and not the setting, so hiding either half takes both lines off, which is the same rule the renderer composites by; (3) no new switch, no flag: the renderer has always skipped a spent layer, so the row telling the truth about it is not a feature to opt into; (4) shortest version that works: one caption line in the slot the pieces and separation notes already use, so no row gets taller.

Built: LayerMaskNote in PhotonzCore (role, matte kind, the other layer's name, the line and the hover), the sibling-list rule moved into PhotonzDocument.matteSource(in:at:)/matteUser(in:at:) so the renderer, the panel and the inspector cannot drift, LayerRowDisplay.maskNote filled in one pass of the tree, and a caption line with an up/down arrow in LayersRow. 19 new core tests, all 9058 tests green. layers-combine-walk now claims both rows in words at 6-matte and claims them plain again after undo; 38 row-touching walks and 11 layers- walks all pass.

left rough, no task filed: (1) three deep, a middle layer is both halves and says only that it is being spent, deliberately, since a layer that is not in the picture at all is the more surprising truth and its own Masked by is changing no pixel; (2) the timeline draws the same layers and its lanes say nothing about a mask, but the Layers list is on screen beside it in the same window, so it is not a person stuck with no answer; (3) the mask row keeps its ordinary thumbnail, which is what the layer IS even though none of it is on the canvas, and it is in the audit as a question for the user.
